subject: Genomex — On‑Prem readiness follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Thompson <mike.thompson@genomex.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Genomex — On‑Prem readiness follow-up & next steps

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete next steps we discussed so the team has a single source of truth. Please flag any corrections.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Deployment mode: Genomex is leaning toward a fully air‑gapped private deployment (on‑prem appliance or VPC‑isolated appliance) for the model runtime. Hosted API and Dedicated were discussed but rejected for regulated workloads.
- Physical constraints: single secure room, limited external network egress (none allowed for inference nodes), rack space limited to 4U x 2 per cluster initially.
- Maintenance windows: preferred monthly maintenance window (local 02:00–05:00) for patching; major upgrades to be scheduled quarterly.
- Encryption & keys: KMS-managed keys acceptable if HSM/KMS can be bridged via approved jump host (we need details).
- Staging & rollback: customer expects a staging instance on isolated hardware and an offline patch process (manual image import + validation) before prod upgrades.

Requested items from Genomex (action items for your side):
1) Network diagram (redacted is fine) showing DMZ, jump hosts, and where the appliance will sit.
2) Target RTO/RPO for inference service and acceptable downtime for quarterly upgrades.
3) Procurement timeline and point of contact (procurement email on the call was procures@genomex.com — I set procure@genomex.com below).
4) Any existing policy on spare parts and onsite spares (we'll propose a spares list).

Our proposed next steps (from Redwood):
- Sean to run a technical deep‑dive on hardware sizing and offline patch flow.
- We will produce an initial airgap readiness checklist (attached) and a proposed staging runbook for your review.
- Schedule a 60‑minute technical session with your infra lead + our infra engineer (Sean) next week.

Attachments: airgap-prelim-checklist.xlsx (prelim checklist, 18 KB)

Thanks — I copied Ben (solutions) and Sean (ops) to pick up technical and procurement coordination. If Asha (infra) or procurement want to join the deep dive please reply with availability.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0137

Subject: Re: Genomex — On‑Prem readiness follow-up & next steps

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Confirmed: air‑gapped appliance in a secure room. No outbound internet from inference nodes.
- We can provide a redacted network diagram by EOD Friday; Asha will own that.
- Maintenance: monthly maintenance window is fine (02:00–05:00 local). For security patches we do prefer an offline image import workflow; please outline the exact steps you recommend.
- Rack space: currently we have 2x 4U slots reserved in the secure rack, can potentially expand by one more 4U if needed.
- Procurement: please include our procurement alias (procure@genomex.com) on any budget/quote emails.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you provide an offline patch playbook (what we install, who signs images, verification steps)?
2) What's the nominal hardware footprint (GPU count) you recommend for a 100 QPS inference baseline with 99th percentile latency <=200ms?
3) If we go with an appliance model, how do you handle firmware OS updates where there's zero external connectivity?

Attachment: initial-site-constraints.pdf (site constraints summary, 26 KB)

I'll loop in Asha and procurement on scheduling. Looking forward to Sean's deep dive.

—Mike
Director of Infrastructure, Genomex

Please confirm which option works or propose alternatives. Sean — can you own the sizing and playbook deliverables? Ben — please prepare a high‑level procurement cost estimate to share with procure@genomex.com after the deep dive.
